long_biography.plain_text:
WestCom began as Michael Hirtenstein's idea for a specialist network serving trading floors. As founder and chief executive, he developed the company into a provider of mission-critical voice and data links for more than 1,200 financial firms. A 2005 investment by One Equity Partners transferred majority ownership while Hirtenstein retained a significant stake and continued guiding expansion into Europe and Asia.

Hirtenstein next applied his dealmaking experience to New York hospitality. He joined Eugene Remm and Mark Birnbaum at EMM Group and shared responsibility for operations, finance and new-property concepts. The group expanded its restaurant and nightlife business around brands including Catch and Lexington Brass, then sold a half-interest to Tilman Fertitta in 2017 to support further growth. He also became known as a real-estate investor, buying, renovating, renting and selling high-end Manhattan and Hamptons properties.
